title: private-cni-reconcile-surge-and-nat-port-starvation-post-incident-action-plan
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary: During a canary rollout of the CNI agent (v2.4.1) to private clusters in eu-west-1 on 2026-03-09 we observed a correlated surge of CNI reconcile loops across node agents. The reconcile invoked an iptables-restore path concurrently on many nodes while the cloud NAT gateway was already near ephemeral port capacity for several high-throughput customers. The combination produced large numbers of TCP reconnects to the control plane, triggering connection backoff and a control-plane partial partitioning that lasted ~45 minutes for affected accounts.

Timeline: 2026-03-09 02:12 UTC - Canary batch started (50 nodes). 02:18 - Increased SYN retries and connection resets observed in agent logs. 02:22 - Grafana alert: control-plane p99 latency spiked from 120ms to 2.1s. 02:28 - Multiple customer agents showed gRPC reconnect storms and token re-auth failures due to race in ephemeral port reuse. 03:00 - Canary paused; rollback attempted but several nodes had iptables restore in-progress; rollback did not fully restore pre-upgrade conntrack state. 03:57 - Control plane recovered after manual intervention (throttling misconfigured, NAT gateway scaling triggered and node-level conntrack tuned).

Primary contributing factors: 1) Upgrade sequencing lacked inter-batch jitter and a reconciliation fence for CNI iptables-restore steps. 2) Centralized NAT gateway design combined with existing high-per-customer egress patterns led to ephemeral source port exhaustion under reconnection spikes. 3) No per-node circuit breaker on gRPC dials or per-customer request shaping at the control-plane ingress. 4) Health-check semantics during iptables-restore briefly presented nodes as healthy while underlying socket state was inconsistent, blocking transparent failover.

Impact: Approximately 7 private customers experienced degraded control-plane connectivity and increased token re-auth failures. Some customer apps observed elevated latency and 5-minute tail errors. Incident window ~45 minutes.

Root cause statement: Simultaneous CNI reconcile-induced socket resets across nodes caused a concentrated surge of outbound connections through a NAT gateway close to ephemeral port limits; control plane lacked ingress shaping and connection-circuiting to absorb the reconnect storm, resulting in partial connectivity loss for private clusters.
comments: 2026-03-10 — Initial incident triage completed. Responsible teams: Private Deployments (owner: Daniel Gómez), Network Reliability (owner: Priya Rao), Runtime (owner: Samir Chen).

2026-03-11 — Infra ran replay of agent logs on staging; reproduced iptables-restore timing causing conntrack bursts when nodes flapped. Recorded script: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PRIV/2026-03-iptables-replay
2026-03-12 — PM review: need business-facing communication for affected customers and SLA credit template drafted (PM: Erin Blake).
2026-03-13 — Design review with Runtime: agreed to add conservative per-node nozzle (rate limiter) and a control-plane side connection adaptor to enforce max concurrent dials per remote IP block.
action_items: AI-1: Implement inter-batch jitter + cluster-level reconcile fence for CNI upgrades to ensure iptables-restore is serialized across nodes. Owner: Daniel Gómez. Estimate: 3 pts. Due: 2026-03-24.

AI-2: Add per-node ephemeral connection rate limiter in the agent that limits simultaneous dial attempts after a reconcile-triggered netstack change. Owner: Samir Chen. Estimate: 4 pts. Due: 2026-03-28.
AI-3: Introduce control-plane ingress circuit breaker per source / per-customer to cap concurrent inbound handshakes and apply exponential backoff. Owner: Priya Rao. Estimate: 5 pts. Due: 2026-04-01.
AI-4: Work with Cloud infra to ensure NAT gateway autoscaling thresholds consider ephemeral port exhaustion (add alert and runbook). Owner: Priya Rao. Estimate: 2 pts. Due: 2026-03-20.
AI-5: Update health-check semantics to verify socket userland consistency post-iptables-restore before marking node healthy. Owner: Daniel Gómez. Estimate: 3 pts. Due: 2026-03-26.
AI-6: Create a small chaos test in staging that simulates rolling iptables-restore across many nodes and validates control-plane stability. Owner: QA (TBD). Estimate: 2 pts. Due: 2026-03-30.
AI-7: Customer comms and SLA review: PM to finalize message and credits for affected customers. Owner: Erin Blake. Estimate: 1 pt. Due: 2026-03-15.
mitigations: Applied temporary throttle on canary upgrades (pause between nodes = 60s).
Scaled NAT gateway pool for impacted accounts and increased ephemeral port range on affected nodes to reduce reuse collisions.
Deployed emergency rule to circuit-break high-rate dialers at edge LB to protect control plane until fix is released.
verification_steps: Run iptables-restore replay in staging with 200-node fanout; validate control-plane p99 latency remains <= 200ms.
Deploy agent dial-rate limiter to a small canary subset and measure egress connection rates and NAT port utilization over 24 hours.
Execute preflight health-check that simulates socket-state mismatch and confirm node is not marked healthy until userland sockets reconcile.
